full_name: National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire-25
domains: 12 subscales: general health, general vision, ocular pain, near activities, distance activities, social functioning, mental health, role difficulties, dependency, driving, colour vision, peripheral vision (optional 14-item appendix)
scoring: each item rescaled 0-100; subscale = mean of items; composite = mean of the 11 vision subscales (general health excluded); Rasch-scaled variants exist
validation_method: CTT; factor analysis; test-retest; internal consistency; Rasch (later studies)
languages: English plus many validated translations (e.g. French, Spanish, Italian, German, Chinese, Japanese); count uncertain
target_population: adults with chronic eye disease (developed in mixed eye-disease samples)
development_citation: Mangione CM, Lee PP, Gutierrez PR, Spritzer K, Berry S, Hays RD. Development of the 25-item National Eye Institute Visual Function Questionnaire. Arch Ophthalmol 2001;119:1050-1058
rasch_validated: yes (several studies; multidimensional and misfitting subscales reported)
field_contrast_coverage: partial: 1-item peripheral vision subscale, night-driving item; no contrast item
short_forms: NEI VFQ-9 (IRT short form); VFQ-25 plus 14-item appendix
notes: Stelmack 2002 (ID 65) Rasch-analysed 34 of 39 items of the VFQ-25 plus supplement in interview format; Selivanova 2019 (ID 72) used 2 Rasch-derived subscales. Verify facts against Mangione 2001 before quoting.

full_name: Veterans Affairs Low-Vision Visual Functioning Questionnaire-48
domains: reading, mobility, visual motor skills, visual information processing (4 subscales); single overall visual-ability measure
response_scale: 4 difficulty categories (not difficult / slightly-moderately / extremely / impossible) plus 'do not do for non-visual reasons' scored missing; three follow-up questions per item
scoring: Rasch (Andrich rating scale model) person measure in logits; subscale scores
languages: English; Italian (Di Maggio 2020); other translations uncertain
administration_mode: telephone interview by trained interviewer (also face-to-face)
target_population: adults with low vision entering vision rehabilitation (developed in US veterans)
development_citation: Stelmack JA, Szlyk JP, Stelmack TR, Demers-Turco P, Williams RT, Moran D, Massof RW. Psychometric properties of the Veterans Affairs Low-Vision Visual Functioning Questionnaire. Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci 2004;45:3919-3928
licence: free (US Department of Veterans Affairs; no licence fee)
scoring_burden: moderate (Rasch scoring table or Winsteps; interviewer training needed)
field_contrast_coverage: partial: mobility and peripheral-detection items reflect field loss indirectly; no contrast item
notes: Time 25-35 min from Stelmack 2006 p5 (ID 66). Szlyk 2004 (ID 74) reports 48 items in navigation, resolution, peripheral detection, finding and general function. Verify development citation.

full_name: Veterans Affairs Low-Vision Visual Functioning Questionnaire-20 (short form)
domains: same construct as VFQ-48 (single visual-ability measure)
development_citation: Stelmack JA, Massof RW. Using the VA LV VFQ-48 and LV VFQ-20 in low vision rehabilitation. Optom Vis Sci 2007;84:705-709
uncertain_fields: all fields: compiled from memory of the development paper; no included study in data/articles_text reports the 20-item form
notes: Mark as unverified until the development paper is read.

n_items: 50 goals; 459 tasks (adaptive: tasks rated only under goals rated important and difficult)
domains: 3 objectives (daily living, social functioning, recreation); 50 goals each with task lists
response_scale: importance (4 categories) then difficulty (5 categories: not difficult to impossible); task difficulty 5 categories or not applicable
scoring: Rasch (Andrich rating scale) person measures for goals and for functional domains (reading, mobility, visual motor, visual information); filtered AI for outcome measurement
time_to_administer_min: 20-30 (uncertain; adaptive, depends on number of important goals); telephone interview including other questionnaires averaged 62 min in Goldstein 2012
administration_mode: telephone or face-to-face interview; computerised adaptive version exists
target_population: adults with low vision referred for rehabilitation
development_citation: Massof RW, Ahmadian L, Grover LL, Deremeik JT, Goldstein JE, Rainey C, Epstein C, Barnett GD. The Activity Inventory: an adaptive visual function questionnaire. Optom Vis Sci 2007;84:763-774
licence: free for academic use from the Lions Vision Research and Rehabilitation Center (confirm with authors)
scoring_burden: high (Rasch scoring; software or author-supplied scoring needed)
field_contrast_coverage: partial: mobility goals and tasks; no field or contrast item as such
short_forms: filtered AI (goal-level ratings only) used as a short outcome measure in Malkin 2013
notes: Massof 2007 (ID 95) describes the 50 goal-level items and the importance-then-difficulty flow (p2). Goldstein 2012 (ID 12) gives the 62-min mean total telephone interview (p2). Malkin 2013 (ID 88) uses the filtered AI.

full_name: Impact of Vision Impairment questionnaire (28-item Rasch version)
domains: reading and accessing information; mobility and independence; emotional well-being (3 subscales; total scale)
response_scale: 4-5 category frequency/difficulty response options (varies by item)
scoring: Rasch person measure per subscale (logits); summed scores in CTT use
languages: English; Dutch, Chinese, Malay, Hindi and others (uncertain)
target_population: adults with vision impairment attending rehabilitation
development_citation: Weih LM, Hassell JB, Keeffe J. Assessment of the impact of vision impairment. Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci 2002;43:927-935 (32-item original); Lamoureux EL, Pallant JF, Pesudovs K, Hassell JB, Keeffe JE. The Impact of Vision Impairment Questionnaire: an evaluation of its measurement properties using Rasch analysis. Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci 2006;47:4732-4741 (28-item)
licence: free for non-commercial use with permission of the Centre for Eye Research Australia (confirm)
scoring_burden: moderate (Rasch conversion table available from authors)
field_contrast_coverage: partial: mobility subscale; no explicit field or contrast item
notes: Selivanova 2019 (ID 72) used the 3 Rasch-scored subscales pre/post rehabilitation (p2).

domains: distance vision, mobility and lighting; adjustment (psychological); reading and fine work; activities of daily living (4 factor-derived sub-sections)
response_scale: 0-5 per item (0 = can no longer do because of vision; 5 = no difficulty) plus not applicable
validation_method: CTT; factor analysis; internal consistency; test-retest (ICC); responsiveness; IRT (Spanish version)
languages: English; Spanish (Perez-Mana 2019/2022); Chinese, Portuguese, Turkish and others (uncertain)
time_to_administer_min: 5-10 (Wolffsohn 2000); 3-7 measured in Perez-Mana 2022 (face-to-face shorter than telephone)
target_population: adults with untreatable vision loss attending low-vision services
development_citation: Wolffsohn JS, Cochrane AL. Design of the low vision quality-of-life questionnaire (LVQOL) and measuring the outcome of low-vision rehabilitation. Am J Ophthalmol 2000;130:793-802
rasch_validated: partial: IRT (generalised partial credit model) for the Spanish version; Rasch of the English original uncertain
licence: free (published in full in the development paper)
field_contrast_coverage: partial: a lighting/glare item in the first sub-section; no field item
notes: Items, scoring, alpha 0.88, reliability 0.72 and 5-10 min from Wolffsohn 2000 (ID 26, p1, p5, p9); Spanish validation facts from Perez-Mana 2022 (ID 119).

domains: central and near vision; peripheral vision; dark adaptation and glare; outdoor mobility (4 factors)
response_scale: 1-5 difficulty (1 = none; 5 = severe) plus 'abstain for non-visual reasons'
scoring: summed score 15-75 (higher = worse); Rasch re-engineered scoring proposed
validation_method: CTT; factor analysis; internal consistency; test-retest; Rasch (later re-analysis)
languages: English; Chinese, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Turkish and others (uncertain)
development_citation: Nelson P, Aspinall P, Papasouliotis O, Worton B, O'Brien C. Quality of life in glaucoma and its relationship with visual function. J Glaucoma 2003;12:139-150
rasch_validated: yes (Khadka 2011 found misfit and multidimensionality; proposed GAL-9)
field_contrast_coverage: yes: peripheral-vision and dark-adaptation/glare factors by design
notes: Not reported by any included study directly; Agathos 2025 (ID 55) used the derived GAL-9. Verify against Nelson 2003.

domains: single visual-ability construct (mobility, peripheral vision, glare and adaptation scenarios)
scoring: Rasch person measure (logits) or summed score
target_population: adults with glaucoma (used in maculopathy by Agathos 2025)
development_citation: Khadka J, Pesudovs K, McAlinden C, Vogel M, Kernt M, Hirneiss C. Reengineering the glaucoma quality of life-15 questionnaire with Rasch analysis. Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci 2011;52:6971-6977
scoring_burden: low-moderate (sum; Rasch table in the paper)
field_contrast_coverage: yes: items chosen for peripheral vision loss and dark adaptation
notes: Agathos 2025 (ID 55, p5): nine activity-scenario questions on a 5-point Likert scale, chosen for short length and mobility focus; developed for peripheral vision loss.

full_name: Andhra Pradesh Eye Disease Study Visual Function Questionnaire
domains: everyday visual tasks grouped by functional demand: resolution, contrast sensitivity, illumination, peripheral vision
response_scale: 0-4 (no difficulty to cannot manage); collapsed to 3 categories after Rasch analysis
scoring: summed score in CTT; Rasch person measure in logits (Gothwal 2012)
languages: Telugu, Hindi, Urdu, English (uncertain beyond Telugu)
target_population: adults with visual impairment in India (population survey origin; rehabilitation-centre validation)
development_citation: Gothwal VK, Bagga DK. Andhra Pradesh Eye Disease Study - Visual Function Questionnaire: further improvements in psychometric properties using Rasch analysis. Ophthalmic Epidemiol 2012;19:313-325 (original: Dandona R et al. 2002)
rasch_validated: yes (not unidimensional overall; four functional subsets)
field_contrast_coverage: yes: items explicitly grouped under contrast sensitivity and peripheral vision
notes: Gothwal 2012 (ID 5, p1-2): 16 items, 0-4 scale, 351 adults, one misfitting item, person separation reliability 0.81, item separation reliability 0.99.

full_name: Melbourne Low-Vision Activities of Daily Living Index
domains: Part A: 16 observed performance tasks (e.g. reading, telling time, pouring); Part B: 9 self-report items
administration_mode: clinician-observed performance plus self-report (not a pure PROM)
development_citation: Haymes SA, Johnston AW, Heyes AD. The development of the Melbourne Low-Vision ADL Index: a measure of vision disability. Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci 2001;42:1215-1225
scoring_burden: high (needs test materials and an observer)
field_contrast_coverage: partial: tasks under different lighting; no field item
notes: Not reported in detail by any included study; cited by Subramanian 2006 (ID 97) and others. Not a self-report screen: performance part needs a clinician.

domains: everyday activities affected by cataract (reading small print, recognising people, seeing steps, driving, etc.)
response_scale: 0-4 difficulty (0 = unable; 4 = no difficulty) plus not applicable
scoring: mean of applicable items x 25 = 0-100 (higher = better)
validation_method: CTT; internal consistency; test-retest; Rasch (VF-8R short form)
target_population: adults with cataract (used widely in other eye disease)
development_citation: Steinberg EP, Tielsch JM, Schein OD, Javitt JC, Sharkey P, Cassard SD, Legro MW, Diener-West M, Bass EB, Damiano AM, Steinwachs DM, Sommer A. The VF-14: an index of functional impairment in patients with cataract. Arch Ophthalmol 1994;112:630-638
field_contrast_coverage: minimal: one night-driving item; no contrast or field item
notes: No included study validates it in a low-vision sample; included only as a comparator many LVR papers cite.

full_name: EQ-5D (3L or 5L) with the vision bolt-on dimension (EQ-5D+V)
domains: mobility, self-care, usual activities, pain/discomfort, anxiety/depression, plus vision
scoring: utility index from a country value set (vision bolt-on value sets exist for the UK 3L); VAS 0-100
validation_method: CTT; responsiveness (Malkin 2013 tested the EQ-5D without bolt-on in LVR)
target_population: general population and all health conditions (generic utility)
development_citation: Longworth L, Yang Y, Young T, et al. Use of generic and condition-specific measures of health-related quality of life in NICE decision-making. Health Technol Assess 2014;18(9):1-224; Yang Y, Rowen D, Brazier J, Tsuchiya A, Young T, Longworth L. An exploratory study to test the impact on three bolt-on items to the EQ-5D. Value Health 2015;18:52-60
licence: registration with the EuroQol Group required; free for non-commercial use
notes: Malkin 2013 (ID 88, p1): EQ-5D (no bolt-on) unresponsive to LVR, ceiling effect (median utility 0.77). Perez-Mana 2022 (ID 119) used EQ-5D-5L as a comparator.

full_name: Legge group 100-item visual acuity survey (self-reported recognition of everyday objects at stated distances)
scoring: IRT (2-parameter logistic) person ability mapped linearly to logMAR; individual items usable as yes/no screens
validation_method: IRT; criterion validity (against measured VA); ROC
target_population: adults 18+ across the full VA range (-0.3 to 2.0 logMAR)
development_citation: Wu Y-H, Yu D, Kwon M, Wang C, Goldstein JE, Legge GE. Estimating visual acuity without a visual acuity chart. Transl Vis Sci Technol 2024 (PMC11412607)
scoring_burden: moderate (IRT scoring) or none for single items
field_contrast_coverage: none: acuity only by design; field and contrast loss with preserved acuity are not captured
short_forms: two-item screen (restaurant menu + keyboard) and single items (Wu 2026)
notes: Wu 2026 (ID 92, p2-3): yes/no items on recognising details at specific distances; IRT difficulties converted to VA thresholds; five items with suboptimal fit; survey 'displayed good reliability' (p3).

full_name: Two screening questions from the 100-item survey: 'In a fast-food restaurant, can you usually read the posted menus?' (low vision, VA 0.3 logMAR) and 'When seated in front of a computer, are you able to read the letters on the keyboard keys?' (legal blindness, 1.0 logMAR)
domains: acuity-dependent recognition at distance and near
scoring: single item: positive if No; pair: rule as published (Wu 2026 Tables 3-4)
validation_method: criterion validity (ROC single point) against measured VA
development_citation: Wu Y-H, Yu D, Goldstein JE, Kwon M, Wang C, Legge GE. Screening questions to identify low vision and acuity-defined legal blindness. Invest Ophthalmol Vis Sci 2026
rasch_validated: no (items selected by AUC from the IRT-calibrated bank)
notes: Wu 2026 (ID 92, p1, p4): menu item AUC 0.85 (sens 0.89, spec 0.81) for VA 0.3 logMAR; keyboard item AUC 0.80 (sens 0.89, spec 0.71) for legal blindness; a second item adds <= 0.05 AUC. AUC is (sens+spec)/2 for a single threshold (p3). Items and cut-offs chosen in the same sample: accuracy goes on the QUADAS-2/DTA path, not COSMIN.

full_name: Single-question self-rated vision (e.g. NHATS: ability to see well enough to recognise someone across the street / read newspaper print with glasses; NHIS: 'Do you have any trouble seeing, even when wearing glasses?'; NHANES/SEE general-vision rating)
response_scale: yes/no or 4-5 category rating (excellent to poor; no trouble to blind)
validation_method: criterion validity (sens/spec) against measured VA in surveys
development_citation: Potter T, et al. Concordance between self-reported visual difficulty and objective visual impairment: the National Health and Aging Trends Study. Ophthalmology 2024
field_contrast_coverage: none: global item; field and contrast loss not captured
uncertain_fields: exact wording per survey; sensitivity/specificity values; development_pmid
notes: Wu 2026 (ID 92, p2) summarises published single-question accuracy (e.g. sensitivity 0.70 / specificity 0.88 for legal blindness; sensitivity 0.25 / specificity 0.92 for a lower threshold); verify each against its primary source before quoting.

domains: independence in daily activities for people with low vision (occupational-therapy outcome)
target_population: adults with low vision in OT-based rehabilitation
development_citation: Smith TM, Pappadis MR, Krishnan S, Reistetter TA. Responsiveness of the Revised Low Vision Independence Measure (LVIM-R). Am J Occup Ther 2020;74:7404205030
notes: Facts need reading of Smith 2013 (ID 85) and Smith 2020 (ID 89) before use.

full_name: Veterans Affairs 13-item self-report blind rehabilitation outcome measure (independence scale)
domains: independence in tasks linked to the four domains of blind rehabilitation skills (orientation and mobility, communication, living skills, manual skills)
scoring: summed independence scale; Rasch person measure in Babcock-Parziale 2005
administration_mode: telephone survey by research staff 4-6 weeks after discharge (retrospective pretest and post-test)
target_population: US veterans discharged from inpatient blind rehabilitation
development_citation: Babcock-Parziale J, McKnight PE, Head DN. Evaluating psychometric properties of a clinical and a self-report blind rehabilitation outcome measure. J Rehabil Res Dev 2005;42:487-498
notes: Babcock-Parziale 2005 (ID 39, p2, p6): 13 items rated 1-3 by telephone; alpha 0.81 (retrospective pretest) and 0.76 (post-test); person reliability 0.71 and 0.27.

full_name: Self-reported mobility performance questionnaire (perceived visual ability for independent mobility; Bibby 2007)
scoring: Rasch rating-scale model (Winsteps) person measure in logits
validation_method: Rasch; criterion validity (correlation with VA and visual field)
development_citation: Bibby SA, Maslin ER, McIlraith R, Soong GP. Vision and self-reported mobility performance in patients with low vision. Clin Exp Optom 2007;90:115-123
field_contrast_coverage: yes: mobility items correlated strongly with binocular visual field (r = -0.76) in Bibby 2007
notes: Row mirrors the data-extraction template (ID 120): 35 items (p4); person reliability 0.93 (p6); correlations with VA 0.41 and with visual field -0.76 (Table 2 p4).

full_name: Visual Impairment as a Risk for Falls Questionnaire
domains: vision-related falls risk in older adults
scoring: summed score with cut-off for falls risk (uncertain)
development_citation: Labreche T, Wilson S, Rabinovitch R, et al. Development and validation of Visual Impairment as a Risk for Falls Questionnaire. Age Ageing 2018;47:xxx
field_contrast_coverage: partial: falls-risk items touch field and contrast (uncertain)
notes: Read Labreche 2018 (ID 27) before using this row; the questionnaire targets falls risk rather than LVR need.
